newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bosnia peace group welcomes local poll delay.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia peace group welcomes local poll delay.

text.p: A key international body overseeing the Bosnian peace process on Friday welcomed a decision by Europe's top security body to put off Bosnia's municipal polls from July to mid-September.

The Peace Implementation Council Steering Board said in a statement released ahead of a key Bosnia conference in Vienna that the elections were of "fundamental importance to the consolidation of long-term peace in Bosnia".
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Thursday it had decided to postpone the local elections to mid-September to allow more time for preparation.
"The Steering Board strongly supports the decision of the OSCE," said the statement released by the office of Carl Bildt, the international High Representative for Bosnia.
"The Steering Board pledges its full support for municipal elections on those dates."
The board comprises representatives of more than 50 states, including the five-power Contact Group, the OSCE and the European Union.

Bosnia's municipal polls were originally to be held in September 1996, along with the general elections, but were postponed because of widespread election fraud over refugee registration to November 1996 and then to July this year.
Western countries funding the election had been pushing for a further postponement of the vote to allow more time to organise refugee registration and international monitoring.

The OSCE's decision on Thursday was strongly criticised by U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen, who called the delay another failure by outside civilian agencies to help rejuvenate the war-shattered country.
